evidence_jobs.title: Head of Platform Engineering
evidence_jobs.quote: ensure the platform can scale to petabytes of security data and billions of daily events

talk_track: This is Daniel Kirichanski — I ran platform engineering at Ripple while it processed over six billion transactions a year, and cut cloud spend 35% doing it, so TENEX's scale problem reads familiar. Your Head of Platform Engineering posting has been open since late January; it asks one person to own SLOs, on-call, MLOps, and a platform that can 'scale to petabytes of security data and billions of daily events.' Six months unfilled usually means the spec is really two jobs stapled together: a data-platform architect and an SRE operator, so every candidate arrives half wrong. Splitting the search — or seating interim platform leadership while it runs — is what protects the SLOs the MDR business is sold on, especially with a $250M Series B funding aggressive hiring on top of that platform. Which half of that role is hurting more right now?
